verdict.rationale: Weave documents automatic capture of inputs and outputs for LLM calls via `@weave.op()` and builds trace trees from them. It also automatically records token usage and cost per call for supported integrations (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Mistral), with custom cost configuration for other models. Latency is never named explicitly; it is only implied by "execution metadata," so the story is not completely covered. missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-call latency/duration capture, automatic token usage for unsupported or self-hosted providers, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: Weave automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata.
this will generate a trace tree of the inputs and outputs of all your functions
Weave automatically records token usage and calculates cost for each call. Costs appear in the trace tree and in the calls table in the Weave UI.
When you call weave.init() and use a supported LLM integration such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, or Mistral, Weave automatically records token usage and calculates cost for each call.
You can trace any function using `weave.op` - from api calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio etc
